stances.claim: The quad comm's televised inquiry has become a popular telenovela -- more lurid and shocking than 'Pulang Araw' or 'Lavender Fields' (which CJ himself watches on Netflix) -- except that the gruesome murders, police connivance, jarring violence, and kitschy sex are real.

Executive Secretary Bersamin's terse 'The Philippines will not return to the ICC' position, joined by House lead co-chair Barbers's refusal to turn over House records, signals the present administration's posture against ICC cooperation.

Solicitor General Guevarra's text to CJ states that the government has no legal duty to cooperate with the ICC investigation because the ICC could no longer exercise jurisdiction over the Philippine situation (Khan was authorized to investigate only in 2021, more than two years after the March 2019 withdrawal took effect) -- though the ICC prosecutor cannot be stopped from interviewing consenting individuals.

Dela Rosa's announced parallel Senate inquiry was blocked by Senate President Escudero's ruling that only the blue ribbon committee can investigate during the Senate break -- though Dela Rosa is confident the former president will attend any Senate hearing.

Leila de Lima is preparing a criminal complaint against Dela Rosa for allegedly coercing quad comm resource person Kerwin Espinosa to link her to the illegal drug trade -- the same coercion that caused her detention for almost seven years before her acquittal.

Those urging ICC Prosecutor Khan to proceed 'may be clapping too soon' because the legislative inquiries, prosecution-office filings, and eventual court trials may themselves negate ICC jurisdiction under Article 17 complementarity (ICC acts only if the state is 'unwilling or unable genuinely to carry out' the case).

Under the Rome Statute, an individual may be held liable only for listed crimes committed in member-state territory or by a member-state national, when the state is or was a member, and without domestic complementarity; and the ICC can assume jurisdiction only over cases initiated within two years of a country's withdrawal. Duterte's withdrawal (notice March 17, 2018; effective March 17, 2019) plus Khan's Sept 15, 2021 authorization (more than two years later) mean the ICC has lost its jurisdiction -- though Bensouda's Feb 8, 2018 preliminary examination is acknowledged in fairness.

one_paragraph_summary: The House quad committee's legislative inquiry on extrajudicial killings, illegal drugs, and POGOs allegedly during Rodrigo Duterte's presidency has become a televised spectacle -- more popular on YouTube and social media than blockbuster telenovelas like GMA's 'Pulang Araw' and ABS-CBN's 'Lavender Fields' (which CJ admits he watches on Netflix every evening except Wednesdays and Thursdays) -- and more lurid and shocking, except that the gruesome murders, police connivance, jarring violence, and kitschy sex are real. Executive Secretary Lucas Bersamin tersely declared 'The Philippines will not return to the ICC,' and quad comm lead co-chair Robert 'Ace' Barbers refused to turn over any records. Solicitor General Menardo I. Guevarra, in a text to CJ, advised the quad comm to refer its findings instead to the DOJ, NBI, or Ombudsman -- and stressed that the government has no legal duty to cooperate with the ICC because Khan was authorized to investigate only in 2021, more than two years after the March 2019 effectivity of the Philippine withdrawal from the Rome Statute, though the ICC prosecutor cannot be stopped from interviewing consenting individuals. Senator Ronald 'Bato' dela Rosa -- stung by what he called unprecedented breaches of interparliamentary courtesy -- announced a parallel Senate inquiry, but Senate President Chiz Escudero limited Senate-break investigations to the blue ribbon committee. Former Senator Leila de Lima is preparing a criminal complaint against Dela Rosa for allegedly coercing quad comm resource person Kerwin Espinosa into linking her to the illegal drug trade, causing her detention for almost seven years before her acquittal. Ironically, ICC supporters 'may be clapping too soon' -- because under Rome Statute Article 17 complementarity, the ICC will act only if the state is unwilling or unable genuinely to prosecute, so the very domestic referrals, prosecutions, and trials may negate ICC jurisdiction. Combined with the two-year-post-withdrawal cap, this means 'ICC has lost its jurisdiction' -- though, in fairness, CJ notes that Bensouda announced her preliminary examination on Feb 8, 2018, and refers readers to his Aug 7, 2023 column for details.
